description: Fix Epic detail page mobile layout: eliminate horizontal overflow, separate title/description from action buttons, display real Epic number in header, and preserve bottom spacing for the mobile bottom nav.

tasks.title: Epic detail page responsive mobile layout
tasks.description: Refactor the Epic detail page header in EpicDetailPage.tsx to a responsive single-column layout on mobile (title/description stacked above action buttons), make the action button group flex-wrap so all buttons stay visible and unclipped, and add flex-wrap to the LinkedIssueRow action container so it doesn't force horizontal overflow at 320px. Desktop layout (md: breakpoint) must remain unchanged. Cover with structural-contract tests for running and idle epic states.
acceptanceCriteria: EpicDetailPage header container uses flex-col on mobile and flex-row at md: breakpoint, so title/description block is above (not beside) the action button group on mobile
Title block retains min-w-0 and occupies full readable width on mobile; long Chinese and long English titles wrap within available width instead of stacking vertically per-character

Action button group uses flex-wrap; primary lifecycle action (Start Epic for idle, Pause for running, Resume for paused) is directly visible; secondary actions (Edit, Mark Done, Close Epic) are reachable without clipping
done and closed epics do not render Start/Pause/Resume lifecycle actions
LinkedIssueRow action container uses flex-wrap so Start/Remove buttons do not force horizontal overflow at 320px
Desktop (>=768px) layout classes restore original flex-row/justify-between single-row arrangement with no regression
npm run typecheck -w packages/web passes
npm run test:run -w packages/web passes, including new mobile layout structural-contract tests for running and idle epic states
tasks.output: packages/web/src/pages/epic-detail/ui/EpicDetailPage.tsx with responsive mobile layout + passing vitest structural-contract tests
tasks.notes: Per design D1/D2/D3: change header container to 'flex flex-col gap-4 md:flex-row md:flex-wrap md:items-start md:justify-between'; keep action group 'flex flex-wrap'; add flex-wrap to LinkedIssueRow action container. jsdom cannot measure scrollWidth/clientWidth — test structural CSS classes and DOM order as proxy per design Risks section.

tasks.title: Header displays real Epic number on project-prefixed routes
tasks.description: Fix the root cause of the bare 'Epic #' header: Header is mounted outside <Routes> so useParams() returns empty. Replace useParams-based epic id lookup with useLocation()-based pathname parsing that extracts the epic id segment from '.../epics/<seg>' patterns, then resolve the number via useEpic(). Show 'Epic #…' while loading, 'Epic #<number>' when loaded, and fall back to a stable short id prefix when no numeric number exists — never bare 'Epic #'.
acceptanceCriteria: Header derives epic id from useLocation().pathname (parsing '.../epics/<segment>') instead of useParams(), working for both /:projectName/epics/:id and legacy /epics/:id routes
Header displays 'Epic #<number>' (e.g. 'Epic #3', 'Epic #12') when the epic has loaded with a number
Header displays 'Epic #…' while the epic is loading
Header never displays bare 'Epic #' when an epic has loaded — falls back to a stable short identifier (id prefix) if no numeric number exists
New test case simulates production mount (Header rendered outside <Routes> but inside router) on a project-prefixed route and asserts 'Epic #<number>' is displayed
Existing header tests continue to pass
npm run typecheck -w packages/web passes
npm run test:run -w packages/web passes, including new production-mount header number test
tasks.output: packages/web/src/widgets/app-shell/ui/Header.tsx with URL-path-derived epic number + passing vitest tests including production-mount scenario
tasks.notes: Per design D4: useLocation() is available anywhere inside the router. Unify the existing duplicate 'firstSegment branch' and 'section branch' epic parsing logic into a single pathname-segment extraction. Do NOT move Header into the route element subtree (rejected alt A).

tasks.title: Preserve bottom spacing for mobile bottom nav with safe-area inset
tasks.description: Fix the shell content container bottom padding in App.tsx so the fixed MobileBottomNav (56px + env(safe-area-inset-bottom)) does not obscure the linked issues region on devices with a home indicator. Change 'pb-14 md:pb-0' to use calc(3.5rem + env(safe-area-inset-bottom)) for the mobile padding.
acceptanceCriteria: App.tsx content container uses bottom padding of calc(3.5rem + env(safe-area-inset-bottom)) on mobile (below md: breakpoint), with md:pb-0 retained for desktop
On devices without a home indicator, env(safe-area-inset-bottom) evaluates to 0 and the padding degrades to 3.5rem (equivalent to current pb-14) with no visual regression
Test asserts the shell container has the calc-based bottom padding class/utility for mobile and pb-0 at md: breakpoint
npm run typecheck -w packages/web passes
npm run test:run -w packages/web passes, including the new bottom-spacing assertion
tasks.output: packages/web/src/app/App.tsx with safe-area-aware bottom padding + passing vitest test
tasks.notes: Per design D5: MobileBottomNav is a shell-level fixed component, so its spacing must be handled at the shell container level, not per-page. Use arbitrary value class 'pb-[calc(3.5rem+env(safe-area-inset-bottom))] md:pb-0'.
